article.title: Hindi to English: Work context sentence
article.description: Hindi: 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है।' English: 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Teaching point: 'करना है' (have to do) is obligation, translated with 'have to' not 'must' here since it's a deadline-driven task obligation, not a personal rule.
article.content: Hindi: 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है।' English: 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Teaching point: 'करना है' (have to do) is obligation, translated with 'have to' not 'must' here since it's a deadline-driven task obligation, not a personal rule.

generated.caption:
Got a work deadline looming? ⏰

To express a task-based obligation, especially when it's deadline-driven like 'करना है', use 'have to'. It's the natural choice for tasks you need to complete by a specific time.

For example: "I have to finish this project by tomorrow." Simple and correct!

Save this tip & share, and follow @EnglishVault for daily lessons!
generated.script: "Mujhe yeh kaam karna hai." Isko English mein 'must' bolte hain ya 'have to'? Aksar log yahaan galti karte hain, right? Dekho, jab bhi koi kaam aapko karna hai because it's a deadline-driven obligation, like office work, tab hum 'have to' use karte hain. 'Must' use karna thoda incorrect ho jaayega. Jaise, 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है' isko hum bolenge 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Yahaan 'have to' shows an obligation related to a task and its deadline. Toh next time jab koi deadline wala kaam ho, always remember to use 'have to'. Ab confusion nahi hogi na? Comment karke batao ye tip aapko already pata thi ya nahi! Aur save kar lo!

slides.body: The Hindi phrase 'मुझे यह प्रोजेक्ट कल तक पूरा करना है' directly translates to 'I have to finish this project by tomorrow.' Here, 'करना है' signifies an obligation, specifically one driven by an external factor like a deadline. While 'must' also expresses obligation, 'have to' is the more natural choice for tasks imposed by circumstances or external requirements. Use 'have to' for deadlines and external duties, reserving 'must' for personal rules or strong internal convictions.
slides.hindiSummary: किसी काम की समय-सीमा या बाहरी बाध्यता बताने के लिए 'have to' का प्रयोग करें, न कि 'must' का।
